#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Delete regular files under DIR older than DAYS days whose names match PATTERN.
# Usage: cleanup.sh [-n] DIR DAYS [PATTERN]
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: cleanup.sh [-n] DIR DAYS [PATTERN]" >&2
  exit 2
}

die() {
  echo "cleanup.sh: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

dry_run=0
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-n" ]]; then
  dry_run=1
  shift
fi

(( $# == 2 || $# == 3 )) || usage
dir=$1
days=$2
pattern=${3:-*}

[[ "$days" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || usage

[[ -n "$dir" ]] || die "refusing to clean an empty directory name"
[[ -d "$dir" ]] || die "not a directory: $dir"

# Canonical paths, so symlinks that point at / or $HOME are refused too.
real=$(cd -P -- "$dir" && pwd -P)
home=""
if [[ -n "${HOME:-}" && -d "$HOME" ]]; then
  home=$(cd -P -- "$HOME" && pwd -P)
fi
if [[ "$real" == / || ( -n "$home" && "$real" == "$home" ) ]]; then
  die "refusing to clean $dir"
fi

# Report paths with the DIR prefix as the caller wrote it.
prefix=$dir
while [[ "$prefix" == */ ]]; do
  prefix=${prefix%/}
done

# find without -L never follows symlinks, and -type f skips them as well.
deleted=$(find -- "$real" -type f -mtime +"$days" -print0 \
  | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
      name=${f##*/}
      if [[ "$name" == $pattern ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$prefix/${f#"$real"/}"
      fi
    done \
  | LC_ALL=C sort)

while IFS= read -r f; do
  [[ -n "$f" ]] || continue
  if [[ "$dry_run" -eq 0 ]]; then
    rm -- "$f"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$f"
done <<< "$deleted"

import os
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts" / "cleanup.sh"
DAY = 86400


def age(path, days):
    t = time.time() - days * DAY
    os.utime(path, (t, t))
    return path


def run(*args, env=None):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(SCRIPT), *args],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        env=env,
    )


@pytest.fixture
def home(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    # Keep the real $HOME out of the way; the script reads HOME for its refusal check.
    home_dir = tmp_path / "home"
    home_dir.mkdir()
    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=str(home_dir))
    return home_dir, env


def test_deletes_old_regular_files_recursively(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    (root / "sub" / "deeper").mkdir(parents=True)
    old = age(root / "old.log", 10)
    old_nested = age(root / "sub" / "deeper" / "n.log", 30)
    fresh = root / "fresh.log"
    fresh.write_text("x")

    result = run(str(root), "5")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == f"{old}\n{old_nested}\n"
    assert not old.exists()
    assert not old_nested.exists()
    assert fresh.exists()


def test_output_is_sorted(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    root.mkdir()
    names = ["c.txt", "a.txt", "b.txt"]
    for name in names:
        age(root / name, 9)

    result = run(str(root), "1")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == "".join(f"{root / n}\n" for n in sorted(names))


def test_dry_run_prints_but_keeps_files(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    root.mkdir()
    old = age(root / "old.txt", 8)

    result = run("-n", str(root), "3")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == f"{old}\n"
    assert old.exists()


def test_pattern_limits_deletion(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    root.mkdir()
    keep = age(root / "keep.txt", 20)
    gone = age(root / "gone.log", 20)

result = run(str(root), "1", "*.log")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == f"{gone}\n"
    assert keep.exists()
    assert not gone.exists()


def test_pattern_uses_shell_glob_on_basename(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    (root / "dir").mkdir(parents=True)
    matched = age(root / "dir" / "file-7.bak", 20)
    other = age(root / "dir" / "file-7.txt", 20)

    result = run(str(root), "1", "file-?.bak")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == f"{matched}\n"
    assert other.exists()
    assert not matched.exists()


def test_directories_are_never_deleted(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    empty = root / "empty"
    empty.mkdir(parents=True)
    age(empty, 40)

    result = run(str(root), "1")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == ""
    assert empty.is_dir()


def test_symlink_in_dir_is_not_deleted_or_followed(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    root.mkdir()
    outside = age(tmp_path / "outside.txt", 50)
    link = root / "link.txt"
    link.symlink_to(outside)

    result = run(str(root), "1")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == ""
    assert link.is_symlink()
    assert outside.exists()


def test_symlinked_directory_contents_are_not_followed(tmp_path):
    root = tmp_path / "work"
    root.mkdir()
    elsewhere = tmp_path / "elsewhere"
    elsewhere.mkdir()
    target = age(elsewhere / "old.txt", 50)
    (root / "linkdir").symlink_to(elsewhere, target_is_directory=True)

    result = run(str(root), "1")

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == ""
    assert target.exists()


def test_paths_are_reported_as_given_under_dir(tmp_path):
    real = tmp_path / "real"
    real.mkdir()
    old = age(real / "old.txt", 10)
    alias = tmp_path / "alias"
    alias.symlink_to(real, target_is_directory=True)

    result = run(str(alias) + "/", "1")

assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout == f"{alias}/old.txt\n"
    assert not old.exists()
